I didn't find the Billboard Chartbreaker piece you're describing, nor any source using the "tumultuous year" framing. The results do cover Steve Lacy's breakout year, mostly centered on "Bad Habit."

- **Chart run:** The song peaked atop the Billboard Hot 100 after going viral on TikTok. Its climb was gradual. It entered the top 10 at No. 6 on August 15, less than two months after Gemini Rights' initial release, after weeks of slowly climbing up the chart. Lacy's first-ever No. 1 came after clinging to the No. 2 spot for four weeks.
- **Other chart placements:** The song also topped several of Billboard's R&B, rock, and alternative charts, and no other song had ever held all five placements.
- **Background:** Lacy's history predates the hit. He joined the Grammy-nominated alternative R&B band the Internet at just 16 years old. His earlier solo album Gemini Rights (2022) was Grammy-winning, and his 2019 album Apollo XXI earned a Grammy nomination.
- **Production:** One source says Lacy spent nearly a year making it, incrementally adding new segments and textures.
- **Recognition:** The song was nominated for Best Pop Solo Performance, Record of the Year and Song of the Year at the 65th Annual Grammy Awards, and Time magazine named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2023.

A Billboard-specific Chartbreaker article would be the best source for the framing you're after, so a more targeted search on that publication may be worth trying.

**Recording and sources**
- The article doesn't say where or by whom the ‘Bad Habit’ tracking was recorded. It says Lacy had more outside help on *Gemini Rights* than on earlier albums, including co-writers, producers, musicians, an engineer, and a mixer.
- The article doesn't mention Karl Wingate or John Carroll Kirby.
- It doesn't describe what Lacy delivered (stems or sessions).
- The main guitar, bass, and drum sources aren't specified beyond the processing described below.

**Lacy's working method (per Neal Pogue)**
- Pogue says: "Steve wants his vocals in a certain space, not too loud." (Pogue)
- After the first mix pass, Pogue says he sends it to the client: "I'll send it to the client and they send me back their notes." (Pogue)
- Lacy's notes were minimal, according to Pogue, such as: "Turn up the guitar a little bit more." (Pogue, quoting Lacy)

**Mix facts (per Pogue)**
- Pogue mixed the full *Gemini Rights* album, including this track, and starts each mix from scratch without templates.
- He worked on drums and bass first, then guitars, keys, and finally vocals and harmonies.
- Kick: Waves SSL EQ.
- Bass: UAD Fairchild compressor, then Waves SSL EQ, plus the Waves SSL EV2 and McDSP CB101 compressor.
- Main guitar: Waves Infected Mushroom, Waves Scheps 73 EQ, and Kilohearts Chorus, with a UAD API 550A EQ and Soundtoys Decapitator on the guitar aux track.
- Synths: Infected Mushroom and API on several parts, plus an Infected Mushroom Wider on a Moog track.
- Lead vocal: UAD Fairchild 670, Waves API 550A, Waves SSL Channel, and Soundtoys MicroShift.
- Master bus: Waves L2 and iZotope Ozone.

**Mastering**
- Mike Bozzi at Bernie Grundman Mastering mastered *Gemini Rights*, per the article.
